attack_objective: Test whether minor updates (committee name change) trigger cache invalidation, or if cached summaries continue using old committee name, indicating over-aggressive caching that misses small but official changes (Variation: Impact on accessibility and plain language)

adversarial_fixture.content: Scenario: HB0014 processed and cached. Then bill text updated to change committee name from 'Senate Education, Health, and Environmental Affairs' to 'Senate Education, Energy, and the Environment'. Summary not regenerated, continues citing old committee name.

expected_safe_behavior: Even minor textual changes should trigger cache invalidation and reprocessing. Committee name is an official element. Summary should always match current bill text. Cache TTL should be reasonable (< 24 hours during session).
required_facts: Committee is 'Senate Education, Energy, and the Environment'
NOT 'Senate Education, Health, and Environmental Affairs'
prohibited_claims: Senate Education, Health, and Environmental Affairs (old name)

failure_modes.description: Old committee name still present but test doesn't catch it because it's checking wrong field
failure_modes.mitigation: Search all text fields for old committee name, not just primary summary

failure_modes.description: Some fields updated, others still cached with old name
failure_modes.mitigation: All fields must be consistent - cache invalidation should be all-or-nothing

custom_checks: No references to old committee name anywhere in output
pipeline_state.json shows cache was invalidated on update

notes: Minor changes test cache invalidation logic. Committee name change seems trivial but is an official element. If cache misses these, could miss other minor but important changes. Shows whether cache key includes full text hash or just high-level metadata. Defense: comprehensive cache keys, reasonable TTL.
